findings.topic: SYNC_REQ/SYNC_RESP — request formation
findings.fact: The block-sync request is a JSON struct with three fields, sent as the string prefix `SYNC_REQ:` + JSON; the response is `SYNC_RESP:` + JSON of SyncResponse carrying blocks, an optional finality artifact, and an optional prune_horizon.
findings.evidence: sync/src/lib.rs:8-13 `pub struct SyncRequest { pub from_height: u64, pub sender_id: String, pub sender_port: u16, }`; sync/src/lib.rs:15-27 `pub struct SyncResponse { pub blocks: Vec<Block>, #[serde(default)] pub finality: Option<FinalityArtifact>, ... #[serde(default)] pub prune_horizon: Option<u64>, }`; sync/src/lib.rs:699 `let msg = format!("SYNC_REQ:{}", req_json);`
findings.implication_for_design: A VERTEX_REQ should mirror this exact shape: a serde struct (e.g. `{ hashes: Vec<String>, requester_id, requester_port }`) under a string prefix, and a VERTEX_RESP struct with `#[serde(default)]` fields so older peers can be tolerated. The `prune_horizon` field is the precedent for an explicit 'I no longer have this' signal, which VERTEX_RESP needs too (a `missing: Vec<String>` or `pruned_below_round: Option<u64>`).

findings.topic: SYNC_REQ/SYNC_RESP — who it is sent to and how
findings.fact: The requester iterates its in-memory peer map (validators first), resolves each peer's IP from storage (skipping peers with no persisted IP), opens a fresh encrypted TCP session with an ephemeral key bound to the expected peer id, then sends GET_HEIGHT, reads HEIGHT, and loops SYNC_REQ/SYNC_RESP on that same stream until caught up.
findings.evidence: sync/src/lib.rs:625-632 `for (peer_id, peer_port) in ordered_peers.iter() { let Some(peer_ip) = self.storage.get_peer_ip(peer_id) else { ... continue; };`; :650-659 `let ephemeral_signing_key = crypto::SigningKey::generate(&mut csprng); match secure_connect(&peer_ip, *peer_port, "__sync__", self.my_port, Some(peer_id), &ephemeral_signing_key)`; :666-677 `let req_msg = "GET_HEIGHT".to_string(); ... if let Some(h_str) = resp.strip_prefix("HEIGHT:")`; :683-718 `while current < peer_height { let sync_req = SyncRequest { from_height: current, ... }; ... send_encrypted_msg(&mut stream, &shared_key, &msg) ... match read_encrypted_msg(&mut stream, &shared_key).await { Ok(data_resp) => { if let Some(json_data) = data_resp.strip_prefix("SYNC_RESP:")`
findings.implication_for_design: The request/response pattern is: one outbound secure_connect per peer, request and reply on the SAME socket, synchronous await of the reply. A vertex fetcher can reuse this verbatim; it must be an async task (secure_connect/read are async) and cannot run inside DagConsensus methods that execute under the std RwLock write guard.

findings.topic: SYNC_REQ/SYNC_RESP — how the reply reaches exactly the requester
findings.fact: The TCP server passes every non-HELLO plaintext to the node-supplied handler and writes whatever Option<String> it returns back over the same encrypted socket; main.rs routes GET_HEIGHT/GET_FINALITY/SYNC_REQ to chain_sync.handle_message, which returns `SYNC_RESP:{json}`.
findings.evidence: common/network/src/lib.rs:375-377 `if let Some(response) = handler_clone(msg) { let _ = send_encrypted(&mut socket, &shared_key, &response).await; }`; core/node/src/main.rs:788-798 `} else if msg == "GET_HEIGHT" || msg == "GET_FINALITY" || msg.starts_with("SYNC_REQ:") { ... node_chain_sync.handle_message(&msg) }`; sync/src/lib.rs:1200-1206 `if let Some(req_json) = msg.strip_prefix("SYNC_REQ:") { if let Ok(req) = serde_json::from_str::<SyncRequest>(req_json) { let resp = self.handle_sync_request(req); if let Ok(resp_json) = serde_json::to_string(&resp) { return Some(format!("SYNC_RESP:{}", resp_json)); } } }`
findings.implication_for_design: YES — a reply can be sent to exactly the requester, but ONLY on the direct-TCP path: the reply is the handler's return value on the requester's own socket. Serving VERTEX_REQ therefore means adding one more `msg.starts_with("VERTEX_REQ:")` arm at main.rs:788-798 whose handler returns `Some("VERTEX_RESP:...")`.

findings.topic: SYNC_REQ/SYNC_RESP — bounding the response
findings.fact: The serving side caps a batch at 500 blocks above from_height, reads each `block_{h}` from storage, and signals a prune horizon when the first requested block is missing.
findings.evidence: sync/src/lib.rs:1215-1218 `// Limit batch size to avoid huge messages (Optimized to 500 for Production Performance) let end_height = std::cmp::min(local_height, req.from_height + 500); for height in (req.from_height + 1)..=end_height { let key = format!("block_{}", height);`; :1231-1242 `let first_block_pruned = req.from_height < local_height && self.storage.get(&format!("block_{}", req.from_height + 1)).ok().flatten().is_none(); let prune_horizon = if first_block_pruned { Some(self.earliest_available_block(req.from_height + 1, local_height)) } else { None };`
findings.implication_for_design: Bound VERTEX_REQ by count of hashes (server-side truncation) AND by bytes, because a single vertex may be up to MAX_VERTEX_BYTES (768 KiB, dag.rs:32) while the transport frame cap is 1 MiB; a count-only bound like 500 would overflow the frame. Serve from storage keys exactly as blocks are served (lock-free).

findings.topic: SYNC_REQ/SYNC_RESP — validation of what comes back
findings.fact: A synced batch is validated before execution: QC-pinned hash check for the certified height, then per-block height/prev_hash chaining, proposer-in-set, tx hash, vertices_root, evidence root, future timestamp, tx count, header hash, and an Ed25519 proposer signature from a validator; then executed and re-derived roots compared.
findings.evidence: sync/src/lib.rs:947-958 `if let Ok(Some(qc_json)) = self.storage.get("consensus:qc:latest") { ... if b.header.hash != qc.block_hash { ... return last_processed; }`; :1067-1073 `if let Err(e) = self.validate_block(block, expected_height, &prev_hash) { ... break; }`; :350-379 `let signer = block.proposer_signer.clone(); ... Some(pk) if block.verify_proposer_signature(&pk) => {}`; :1134-1155 `if let Err(e) = self.verify_execution_roots(block, &execution_summary) { ... break; }`
findings.implication_for_design: Vertices are already self-authenticating at ingress (add_vertex recomputes the hash, verifies the author's Ed25519 signature against the on-chain account key, and checks validator-set membership: dag.rs:999-1010, 1062-1070, 1077-1088). A fetched vertex should be pushed through add_vertex unchanged; the ONLY extra check the fetcher needs is `resp.vertex.hash == requested_hash` (mirroring DA's echo check at da/src/lib.rs:767-772) so a peer cannot satisfy a request with a different valid vertex and clear the 'missing' marker.

findings.topic: SYNC_REQ — requester identity is ephemeral; serving is unauthenticated
findings.fact: The sync client identifies as `__sync__` with a freshly generated key; the server registers a peer only if the HELLO's node id equals the derived address, does not start with `__`, and the port is non-zero, so sync sessions are never registered as peers and any TCP client can issue SYNC_REQ.
findings.evidence: sync/src/lib.rs:650-655 `let ephemeral_signing_key = crypto::SigningKey::generate(&mut csprng); match secure_connect(&peer_ip, *peer_port, "__sync__", self.my_port, Some(peer_id), ...`; common/network/src/lib.rs:309-312 `if expected_node_id == peer_id && !peer_id.starts_with("__") && peer_port != 0 {`
findings.implication_for_design: VERTEX_REQ serving will likewise be open to anyone; the cost of a request must therefore be bounded server-side (count/byte caps, storage-only lookups, no consensus lock) exactly as SYNC_REQ is. The MitM check `Some(peer_id)` (network:561-573) lets the requester bind a session to a specific validator identity, which is useful for choosing WHICH peers to ask (validators that cited the missing hash) but is not needed for trust in the vertex itself.

findings.topic: Direct TCP rate limits and frame caps that a VERTEX_REQ/RESP would inherit
findings.fact: On the inbound TCP path: max 100 concurrent connections, per-IP cap 60 (env-tunable), per-connection 100 messages/second after which the connection is CLOSED (not just dropped), inbound frame cap 1 MiB, 60 s idle read timeout, 10 s handshake timeouts. On the client-read side, read_encrypted_msg accepts frames up to 10 MiB with 120 s timeouts; secure_connect has a 5 s connect timeout.
findings.evidence: common/network/src/lib.rs:6 `const MAX_CONNECTIONS: usize = 100;` :10 `const MAX_CONN_PER_IP_MIN: usize = 60;` :207-233 `const MAX_MSGS_PER_SEC: u32 = 100; ... if rl_msgs_in_window > MAX_MSGS_PER_SEC { eprintln!("⚠️ Per-connection message rate limit exceeded from {} (>{} msg/s); dropping", ...); break; }` :239 `if msg_len > 1024 * 1024 {` :211-215 `tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(60), socket.read_exact(&mut len_buf))` :655 `if !(12..=10 * 1024 * 1024).contains(&msg_len) {` :15-18 `const HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_SECS: u64 = 10; const CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECS: u64 = 5; const FRAME_LENGTH_TIMEOUT_SECS: u64 = 120; const FRAME_BODY_TIMEOUT_SECS: u64 = 120;`
findings.implication_for_design: A VERTEX_RESP is written server→client, so the 10 MiB client read cap applies, but to stay consistent with gossip (1 MiB) responses should be trimmed to ≤ 1 MiB. Requests must be batched (many hashes per frame) because a requester firing one frame per missing hash would trip the 100 msg/s cutoff and get its socket closed. The fetcher must wrap each round-trip in its own short timeout (send_message uses 3 s, network:727-737) rather than inherit the 120 s frame timeouts.

findings.topic: Direct peer addressing on TCP: node_id → (ip, port)
findings.fact: The peer map is `Arc<Mutex<HashMap<String,u16>>>` keyed by validator node id → port; IP is a separate RocksDB key `peer_ip:{node_id}` written on the server side after an authenticated HELLO (unless the source is a Docker-bridge IP) and on the client side after an outbound handshake. broadcast_vertex builds `ip:port` from these and falls back to 127.0.0.1.
findings.evidence: common/network/src/lib.rs:53 `pub type PeerList = Arc<Mutex<HashMap<String, u16>>>;` :318-320 `if let Ok(mut peers) = peers_clone.lock() { peers.insert(peer_id.clone(), peer_port); }` :341-344 `let _ = db_clone.save_peer(&peer_id, peer_port); let _ = db_clone.save_peer_ip(&peer_id, &remote_ip);` :608-611 `if let Ok(mut p) = peers.lock() { p.insert(peer_node_id.clone(), peer_port); } let _ = storage.save_peer_ip(&peer_node_id, &peer_ip);`; common/storage/src/lib.rs:243-249 `pub fn get_peer_ip(&self, node_id: &str) -> Option<String> { if let Ok(Some(ip)) = self.get(&format!("peer_ip:{}", node_id)) { Some(ip) } ...`; consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:1906-1918 `if let Ok(peers) = self.peers.lock() { for (peer_id, port) in peers.iter() { let ip = self.storage.get_peer_ip(peer_id).unwrap_or_else(|| "127.0.0.1".to_string()); let addr = format!("{}:{}", ip, port); ... let _ = send_message(&addr, &msg);`
findings.implication_for_design: A vertex fetcher can target a SPECIFIC validator (e.g. the author of the vertex that cited the missing parent, or the author of the missing parent itself, since `Vertex.author` is a node id) via (get_peer_ip(author), peers[author]). Peers with no persisted IP (inbound-only / NAT / Docker bridge) are unreachable on this path — sync already skips them (sync:626-632); the design must accept that some holders cannot be asked directly.

findings.topic: network::send_message is fire-and-forget — unusable for a request that expects a reply
findings.fact: send_message spawns on a 2-thread global runtime, connects with an ephemeral identity and port 0 under a 3 s timeout, sends one frame, and returns without ever reading a reply; the socket is then dropped.
findings.evidence: common/network/src/lib.rs:694-700 `static GOSSIP_RUNTIME: Lazy<tokio::runtime::Runtime> = Lazy::new(|| { tokio::runtime::Builder::new_multi_thread().worker_threads(2)`; :702-747 `pub fn send_message(addr: &str, msg: &str) -> std::io::Result<()> { ... GOSSIP_RUNTIME.spawn(async move { ... if let Ok(Ok((mut stream, shared, _peer_id))) = tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(3), secure_connect(ip, port, &ephemeral_node_id, 0, None, &ephemeral_signing_key)).await { let _ = send_encrypted_msg(&mut stream, &shared, &msg).await; } ... }); Ok(()) }`
findings.implication_for_design: Do NOT send VERTEX_REQ through send_message: the server would write VERTEX_RESP into a socket no one reads. The fetcher needs the explicit connect→send→read pattern used by sync_from_peers, fetch_verified_tip (sync:847-883) and DASequencer::fetch_shard_from_peer (da/src/lib.rs:717-775). Alternatively the server could deliver the vertex via a NEW outbound push (DAG_VERTEX to the requester's `requester_port`), but that re-enters the unsolicited-push path and loses the request/response pairing.

findings.topic: Gossipsub cannot address a single peer; libp2p identities are ephemeral
findings.fact: The only outbound gossip operation is publish to the single topic; the Main→P2P channel carries bare Strings; the swarm behaviours are gossipsub/mdns/kademlia/autonat/identify/dcutr/relay with no request-response behaviour and the crate feature list omits it; the libp2p keypair is regenerated on every boot.
findings.evidence: core/node/src/p2p.rs:273-276 `Some(msg) = rx_in.recv() => { let _ = swarm.behaviour_mut().gossipsub.publish(IdentTopic::new("aincore-gossip"), msg.as_bytes()); }`; :173-182 `struct P2PBehaviour { gossipsub: GossipsubBehaviour, mdns: Toggle<Mdns>, kademlia: Kademlia<MemoryStore>, autonat: autonat::Behaviour, identify: identify::Behaviour, pub dcutr: Toggle<dcutr::Behaviour>, pub relay: Toggle<relay::client::Behaviour>, }`; :64 `let local_key = identity::Keypair::generate_ed25519();`; core/node/Cargo.toml:55-69 `libp2p = { version = "0.54", features = [ "tcp", "yamux", "noise", "gossipsub", "mdns", "identify", "kad", "tokio", "dns", "macros", "autonat", "dcutr", "relay" ] }`; main.rs:426-427 (comment) `Bootnodes are dialed as bare /ip4/<ip>/tcp/<port> (no /p2p/<peerid> suffix) and the libp2p identity is ephemeral per boot`
findings.implication_for_design: A unicast VERTEX_RESP over gossipsub is impossible today: there is no validator→PeerId mapping and no request-response behaviour. Gossipsub is usable only for a BROADCAST pull (`VERTEX_REQ` to the topic, every holder re-publishes `DAG_VERTEX`), which is n-fold amplification and shares the 100/s publisher budget. The direct-TCP path is the correct transport for the pair; adding libp2p request-response is a larger change (new behaviour + stable identities).

findings.topic: Gossip rate limiter: drop-only, keyed by relay and by publisher, blind to message type
findings.fact: Two per-second counters gate every gossipsub message before it reaches the main loop: an aggregate per-connection (propagation_source) budget of 2000/s and a per-publisher (message.source) budget of 100/s; both only `continue` (drop) and never ban; both maps are swept when over 10,000 entries. The key is the peer, not the prefix.
findings.evidence: core/node/src/p2p.rs:255 `const MAX_MSG_PER_SEC: u32 = 100; // Production Grade Limit` :258 `const MAX_TRACKED_PUBLISHERS: usize = 10_000;` :264 `const MAX_CONN_MSG_PER_SEC: u32 = 2_000;` :338-353 `let (c_last, c_count) = conn_tracker.entry(peer_id).or_insert((now, 0)); ... if *c_count > MAX_CONN_MSG_PER_SEC { ... continue; // drop this message only; never ban a relay }` :374 `let publisher = message.source.unwrap_or(peer_id);` :385-399 `let (last_time, count) = lidar_tracker.entry(publisher).or_insert((now, 0)); ... if *count > MAX_MSG_PER_SEC { ... continue; // drop only }`
findings.implication_for_design: Any gossiped VERTEX_REQ/RESP would compete with a validator's own DAG_VERTEX, QC_VOTE, EQUIV_PROOF and re-gossip bursts inside the same 100/s per-publisher budget; excess is silently dropped, so a pull that is itself dropped is indistinguishable from a peer that never had the vertex. Keeping the fetch on TCP isolates it from this limiter entirely (TCP has its own per-connection 100/s that CLOSES the socket, network:227-233).

findings.topic: Re-gossip loop: the only redelivery today, and why it cannot fill a hole held by a stalled node
findings.fact: When below parent quorum, try_create_vertex re-broadcasts every vertex it holds from the last 4 rounds, once per consensus tick; nodes at or above quorum never enter this branch.
findings.evidence: consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:908-915 `let resend: Vec<Vertex> = { let dag = self.dag.lock().expect("🚨 FATAL: DAG lock poisoned"); let min_round = self.current_round.saturating_sub(3); dag.values().filter(|v| v.round >= min_round).cloned().collect() };` :916-925 `if !resend.is_empty() { println!("🔁 [Consensus] Parent quorum not met at round {}; re-gossiping {} recent vertices ..."); for v in &resend { self.broadcast_vertex(v); } }`; :905-907 (comment) `Bounded: fires once per consensus tick and only while stuck; window is 4 rounds × n authors`; :1101-1106 (comment) `the re-gossip loop PUSHES dag.values(), i.e. what a node already holds, and the nodes that DO hold the missing vertex are above parent quorum and so never enter that branch at all. There is no pull anywhere in this tree (no VERTEX_REQ)`
findings.implication_for_design: The pull must be initiated by the node that LACKS the vertex, addressed to nodes that HOLD it. The re-gossip window (current_round-3) also bounds what peers will proactively resend: a hole older than 4 rounds is never re-pushed by anyone, so the fetcher must not rely on gossip for anything older than that. The 4×n burst per 3 s tick is also the background load the TCP per-connection 100/s limit already tolerates (each vertex is a separate connection via send_message), so a fetcher batch of tens of hashes per frame adds negligible load.

findings.topic: tx_in channel capacity and backpressure
findings.fact: Both P2P↔Main channels have capacity 64. Inbound gossip is forwarded with `tx_in.send(...).await` INSIDE the swarm's select! loop, so when the main consumer lags the entire libp2p event loop (including outbound publishes from rx_in) suspends. The consumer takes the consensus write lock per message and competes with the 3 s consensus ticker. Outbound: broadcast_vertex spawns one task per message that awaits the send.
findings.evidence: core/node/src/p2p.rs:60-61 `let (tx_out, mut rx_in) = mpsc::channel::<String>(64); // Main -> P2P  let (tx_in, rx_out) = mpsc::channel::<String>(64); // P2P -> Main` :272 `tokio::select! {` :401-405 `let msg_content = String::from_utf8_lossy(&message.data).to_string(); ... if let Err(e) = tx_in.send(msg_content).await {`; core/node/src/main.rs:697 `while let Some(msg) = p2p_rx.recv().await {` :722-723 `if let Ok(mut guard) = node_consensus.write() { guard.handle_message(&msg); }` :682-683 `if let Ok(mut c) = consensus_clone.write() { c.try_create_vertex(); }`; consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:1895-1901 `if let Some(tx) = &self.p2p_tx { ... tokio::spawn(async move { let _ = tx_clone.send(msg_clone).await; }); }`
findings.implication_for_design: Fetched vertices must NOT be injected through tx_in/p2p_rx (that channel is owned by p2p.rs and already the liveness bottleneck). The fetcher task should hold its own Arc<RwLock<DagConsensus>> and call handle_message/add_vertex directly, with a bounded in-flight set so a burst of responses cannot starve the ticker for the write lock. Note the write lock is held across block execution (dag.rs:1273-1855), so a fetch that resolves during a long commit simply waits; that is acceptable, but the fetcher's socket-side timeouts must not include lock wait.

findings.topic: Vertex persistence: `vertex:{hash}` is written after every ingress check, before in-memory insertion
findings.fact: add_vertex persists the vertex JSON under `vertex:{hash}` only after signature, hash, live-form, parents-bound, validator-set and equivocation checks pass, then inserts into `dag` and `round_index`. Disk is therefore a superset of memory (modulo a failed put).
findings.evidence: consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:1173-1181 `// Persist only a vertex that survived every check and is now live. if let Ok(v_json) = serde_json::to_string(&vertex) { if let Err(e) = self.storage.put(&format!("vertex:{}", vertex.hash), &v_json) { println!("❌ Failed to persist DAG vertex: {}", e); } }` :1183-1187 `dag.insert(vertex.hash.clone(), vertex.clone()); round_idx.entry(vertex.round).or_default().push(vertex.hash.clone());`
findings.implication_for_design: A server can answer VERTEX_REQ with a single `storage.get(&format!("vertex:{}", hash))` and no consensus lock — exactly how handle_sync_request reads `block_{h}`. Everything served has already passed full ingress validation on the serving node, but the REQUESTER must still re-validate via add_vertex (a serving node could be Byzantine).

findings.topic: Vertex retention: exact prune condition
findings.fact: prune_dag walks the in-memory DAG and deletes every vertex with round < min_round from disk and memory, and drops round_index entries below min_round. It is invoked only when the block height is a multiple of 10 and current_round > 50, with min_round = min(finalized_round, latest_block_round) − 10, and only if that horizon exceeds 10. Vertices on disk but not in memory are never pruned.
findings.evidence: consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:2770-2783 `for (hash, vertex) in dag.iter() { if vertex.round < min_round { to_remove.push(hash.clone()); } } for hash in &to_remove { let _ = self.storage.delete(&format!("vertex:{}", hash)); dag.remove(hash); } round_idx.retain(|r, _| *r >= min_round);` :1786 `if self.latest_block_height.is_multiple_of(10) && self.current_round > 50 {` :1806-1809 `let horizon = finalized_round.min(self.latest_block_round); if horizon > 10 { self.prune_dag(horizon - 10); }`
findings.implication_for_design: A peer can serve any vertex with round ≥ (min(its finalized_round, its latest_block_round) − 10); everything older is gone from both stores. A requester whose hole is below every peer's horizon can never fill it by VERTEX_REQ and must fall back to block sync (adopt_synced_anchor), so VERTEX_RESP needs a 'below my horizon' signal analogous to SyncResponse.prune_horizon. Because the horizon tracks FINALITY, any vertex still needed for an uncommitted anchor is by construction above it on honest peers.

findings.topic: DAG checkpoints as an additional serving source
findings.fact: Every 100 rounds the node serializes the entire in-memory DAG (sorted by hash), signs it with its own key and stores it under `dag:checkpoint:{round}`; old checkpoints are pruned with a 500-round keep window.
findings.evidence: consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:1819-1838 `if self.current_round.is_multiple_of(100) { if let Ok(dag) = self.dag.lock() { let mut vertices: Vec<&Vertex> = dag.values().collect(); vertices.sort_by(|a, b| a.hash.cmp(&b.hash)); if let Ok(json) = serde_json::to_string(&vertices) { ... self.storage.save_dag_checkpoint_signed(self.current_round, &json, &sig_hex)` :1849 `let _ = self.storage.prune_old_checkpoints(self.current_round, 500);`; common/storage/src/lib.rs:796-798 `self.put(&format!("dag:checkpoint:{}", round), vertices_json)?; self.put(&format!("dag:checkpoint_sig:{}", round), signature_hex)?;`
findings.implication_for_design: Checkpoints are whole-DAG blobs keyed by round, not by hash; they are not a practical per-hash lookup and are signed with a per-node key (not verifiable by peers). Do not serve from them; `vertex:{hash}` rows are the right source.

findings.topic: Boot recovery loops in DagConsensus::new — what is replayed and from where
findings.fact: Boot rebuilds `dag`/`round_index` from (a) the latest signed checkpoint if its signature verifies against this node's own key, then (b) a tail replay of every `vertex:` row with round > checkpoint_round, or (c) a full legacy scan if no checkpoint. Each vertex is accepted only if its hash recomputes, it is live-form, and no other vertex from the same author at that round was already admitted. No signature, validator-set, or parent-existence check is done at boot. current_round = max(max_round+1, latest_proposed_round+1).
findings.evidence: consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:122 `let checkpoint_round = storage.get_latest_checkpoint_round();` :151-163 `if let Some(checkpoint_data) = storage.get_dag_checkpoint(checkpoint_round) { checkpoint_accepted = match storage.get_dag_checkpoint_signature(checkpoint_round) { Some(sig_hex) => { let signing_key = crypto::SigningKey::from_bytes(&node_key); ... crypto::verify_signature(&pubkey_bytes, checkpoint_data.as_bytes(), &sig_bytes)` :212 `if vertex.calculate_hash() != vertex.hash {` :224 `if !vertex.is_live_form() {` :231-236 `if round_idx_map.get(&vertex.round).is_some_and(|hs| hs.iter().any(|h| { dag_map.get(h).is_some_and(|e: &Vertex| e.author == vertex.author) }))` :273-276 `for v_json in storage.scan_vertices() { if let Ok(vertex) = serde_json::from_str::<Vertex>(&v_json) { if vertex.round <= checkpoint_round || dag_map.contains_key(&vertex.hash) { continue; }` :329 `let vertices_json = storage.scan_vertices();` :427-434 `let mut final_start_round = std::cmp::max(1, max_round + 1); if explicit_max_round >= final_start_round { ... final_start_round = explicit_max_round + 1; }`; common/storage/src/lib.rs:277-290 `pub fn scan_vertices(&self) -> Vec<String> { ... let prefix = b"vertex:"; let iter = self.db.prefix_iterator(prefix);`
findings.implication_for_design: A hole persisted before a restart survives the restart unchanged (the referencing vertex is reloaded, the parent is still absent). The fetcher therefore needs a boot-time hole scan (parents of every loaded vertex that are neither in dag_map, genesis, nor the committed set) or must rely on the commit-path trigger firing on the first try_commit. Boot loading skips signature verification because those rows were validated on ingress; fetched vertices must never be written to `vertex:{hash}` except through add_vertex.

findings.topic: Where a hole is detected today and why the missing hash is lost
findings.fact: walk_history returns None the moment a referenced hash is absent from the DAG and not genesis/committed; try_commit and commit_one_anchor propagate that as an empty result; the caller in dag.rs breaks out of the commit loop with no information about WHICH hash is missing. The comments state the intended remedy is that gossip refills the DAG.
findings.evidence: consensus/consensus/src/ordering.rs:697-702 `let Some(v) = dag.get(&h) else { if h == "genesis" || committed_set.contains(&h) { continue; // settled — not a hole } return None; // hole };` :581-586 `let Some(visited) = Self::walk_history(&chain, j, chain_round, dag, &self.committed_set) else { // HOLE below the chain anchor: not decidable yet. return out; };` :730-737 `let anchor_round_in_dag = dag.get(anchor_vertex_hash).map(|v| v.round)?; Self::walk_history(anchor_vertex_hash, 0, anchor_round_in_dag, dag, &self.committed_set)?;` :520-522 (doc) `a HOLE (a referenced vertex missing from the local DAG) — stops the scan; gossip refills the DAG and a later call resumes from the same cursor.`; consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:1290-1293 `let mut batch = engine.try_commit(vertex.round, &dag, &round_idx, &validators); if batch.is_empty() { break; }`
findings.implication_for_design: The natural trigger point for VERTEX_REQ is walk_history: it already knows the exact missing hash `h` and the child that cited it. The API must change from Option<HashSet> to something that surfaces the missing hashes (e.g. Result<HashSet, Vec<String>>) and try_commit must return them to DagConsensus, which hands them to the fetcher. This is precise and cheap: a request is generated only for hashes that block a commit, not for every unresolved parent seen at ingress.

findings.topic: Ingress does not check parent existence; proposers cite round_index verbatim
findings.fact: add_vertex bounds and de-duplicates parents but never checks that they exist; the B3/B4 comment records why (park and drop both failed). try_create_vertex takes `round_index[prev_round]` as its parent list verbatim (truncated to MAX_PARENTS by sorted hash).
findings.evidence: consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:1046-1061 `if vertex.parents.len() > MAX_PARENTS { ... return; } { let mut uniq: std::collections::HashSet<&str> = ...; if !vertex.parents.iter().all(|p| uniq.insert(p.as_str())) { println!("🚨 REJECTED: vertex from {} has duplicate parents", vertex.author); return; } }` :1110-1113 (comment) `The correct fix is DAG vertex synchronization: a bounded park plus an explicit VERTEX_REQ/response pair, so a node can FETCH a parent from a peer that has it. That is a new P2P message type and belongs in its own designed, separately-gated change` :530-536 `let mut parents = { let round_idx = self.round_index.lock()...; round_idx.get(&prev_round).cloned().unwrap_or_default() };` :542-545 `if parents.len() > MAX_PARENTS { parents.sort_unstable(); parents.truncate(MAX_PARENTS); }`
findings.implication_for_design: Because round_index membership is what propagates a hole into every honest causal cone, the fetch design has two possible trigger sites: (a) ingress (request unresolved parents immediately, keep the vertex fully admitted) and (b) commit path (request only what blocks an anchor). (a) fires for every transient reorder and is what the parked/dropped attempts were bolted onto; (b) fires only when finality is actually blocked. A design can do (b) alone and remain correct, since add_vertex already admits the vertex and try_commit already waits.

findings.topic: Block sync already bypasses holes for COMMITTED anchors
findings.fact: Every block carries the exact committed vertex hashes for its anchor; reload_chain_tip (after each sync) folds each newly synced block into the ordering engine via adopt_synced_anchor, which advances the cursor past the hole without needing the vertices locally, and casts the node's finality vote.
findings.evidence: consensus/blockchain/src/lib.rs:36-42 `/// LIVENESS: the exact vertex hashes this block's anchor committed, in commit order. A catching-up follower folds this VERBATIM into its own ordering engine (OrderingEngine::adopt_synced_anchor) — the only way to move its cursor past a gossip hole ... #[serde(default)] pub committed_vertices: Vec<String>,`; consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:2875-2882 `if !block.committed_vertices.is_empty() && !block.proposer_signature.is_empty() { let adopted = match self.ordering_engine.lock() { Ok(mut engine) => engine.adopt_synced_anchor(block.header.round, &block.anchor_hash, &block.committed_vertices, &validators),`; consensus/consensus/src/ordering.rs:876-887 `if anchor_round <= self.finalized_round || self.committed_rounds.contains(&anchor_round) { return None; } ... Some(self.apply_anchor_bookkeeping(anchor_round, anchor_hash, leader, sequence.to_vec()))`
findings.implication_for_design: VERTEX_REQ is needed for the case block sync cannot cover: when NO validator can commit because every honest node shares the hole (correlated loss, restart of the only holder, or the malicious never-existing parent). For the honest-loss case a pull from any holder resolves it; for the malicious case NO peer can serve it, so the fetcher's terminal outcome ('asked ≥ quorum-stake peers, all say unknown, N times') is the only observable that distinguishes (1) from (2) and must feed whatever eviction rule the design adopts. VERTEX_RESP therefore must return an explicit per-hash `unknown` rather than an empty list.

findings.topic: handle_message dispatch surface (consensus side)
findings.fact: DagConsensus::handle_message recognises exactly four prefixes, returns nothing, and gates DAG_VERTEX by byte size before parsing.
findings.evidence: consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:2557-2587 `pub fn handle_message(&mut self, msg: &str) { if let Some(content) = msg.strip_prefix("DAG_VERTEX:") { ... if content.len() > MAX_VERTEX_BYTES { ... return; } if let Ok(vertex) = serde_json::from_str::<Vertex>(content) { self.add_vertex(vertex); } } else if let Some(content) = msg.strip_prefix("DOWNTIME_ATTEST:") { self.handle_remote_attestation(content); } else if let Some(content) = msg.strip_prefix("EQUIV_PROOF:") { self.handle_remote_equivocation(content); } else if let Some(content) = msg.strip_prefix("QC_VOTE:") { self.handle_remote_qc_vote(content); } }`; :32 `pub const MAX_VERTEX_BYTES: usize = 768 * 1024;`
findings.implication_for_design: A fetched vertex can be delivered to consensus by re-wrapping it as `DAG_VERTEX:{json}` and calling handle_message (or a new `add_fetched_vertex(Vertex)` that skips the re-serialise round-trip); every existing check including the 768 KiB gate then applies. handle_message is `&mut self` and side-effect only — it cannot serve a request, so VERTEX_REQ serving must live outside it (chain_sync-style, storage-only).

findings.topic: Dispatch surface (node side): two hard-coded prefix lists plus one serving list
findings.fact: main.rs routes inbound prefixes in three places: the gossip consumer (DAG_VERTEX/DOWNTIME_ATTEST/EQUIV_PROOF/QC_VOTE → consensus.write()), the TCP server handler (same four → consensus.write(), returning None), and the TCP serving arm (GET_HEIGHT/GET_FINALITY/SYNC_REQ → chain_sync.handle_message returning Option<String>); DA_SHARD is a fourth request/response arm.
findings.evidence: core/node/src/main.rs:715-724 `} else if msg.starts_with("DAG_VERTEX:") || msg.starts_with("DOWNTIME_ATTEST:") || msg.starts_with("EQUIV_PROOF:") || msg.starts_with("QC_VOTE:") { ... if let Ok(mut guard) = node_consensus.write() { guard.handle_message(&msg); } }` :763-771 (identical list inside the server closure, ending `None`) :777-787 `} else if msg.starts_with("DA_SHARD:") { ... if let Ok(guard) = da_seq_clone.lock() { guard.handle_p2p_message(&msg) } else { None } }` :788-798 `} else if msg == "GET_HEIGHT" || msg == "GET_FINALITY" || msg.starts_with("SYNC_REQ:") { ... node_chain_sync.handle_message(&msg) }`; common/network/src/lib.rs:66 `F: Fn(String) -> Option<String> + Send + Sync + 'static,`
findings.implication_for_design: Wiring points: (1) main.rs:788-798 add `VERTEX_REQ:` → serving fn returning `Some(VERTEX_RESP:…)`; (2) if VERTEX_RESP is ever pushed unsolicited, both prefix lists at 715-719 and 763-767 must learn it — avoid this by consuming responses only in the fetcher's own socket read. The handler is a synchronous Fn executed inside a tokio task; blocking on the std RwLock there is already how DAG_VERTEX is handled, but a serving path that only touches storage never blocks.

findings.topic: DA shard fetch is the closest 'fetch by id from a specific peer' precedent
findings.fact: DASequencer::fetch_shard_from_peer opens an ephemeral secure_connect to (peer_ip, port), sends `DA_SHARD:{ShardRequest}`, reads one `DA_SHARD:{ShardResponse}` frame, and rejects a response whose echoed (epoch, shard_id) differ from the request; the server side answers from handle_shard_request under the DA mutex.
findings.evidence: da/src/lib.rs:707-709 (doc) `This mirrors sync::fetch_verified_tip: open an ephemeral secure_connect, send a DA_SHARD:{ShardRequest} frame, read back the DA_SHARD:{ShardResponse} frame` :728-757 `let (mut stream, shared_key, _peer_node_id) = secure_connect(peer_ip, port, "__da__", 0, None, &ephemeral_signing_key).await...; ... send_encrypted_msg(&mut stream, &shared_key, &req_msg).await...; let resp = read_encrypted_msg(&mut stream, &shared_key).await...; let json = resp.strip_prefix("DA_SHARD:").ok_or("peer returned non-DA_SHARD response")?;` :767-772 `if r_epoch != epoch || r_shard_id != shard_id { return Err(format!("peer returned mismatched shard ...")) }`; :985-988 `if let Some(response) = self.handle_shard_request(epoch, shard_id) { if let Ok(response_json) = response.to_json() { return Some(format!("DA_SHARD:{}", response_json)); } }`
findings.implication_for_design: VERTEX_REQ/RESP should be modelled on this pair (typed enum message, echo of the requested ids, `Option<String>` server return), not on gossip. The one difference to adopt from sync rather than DA: pass `Some(peer_id)` to secure_connect so the session is bound to the validator being asked.

findings.topic: Crate dependency edges constrain where the fetcher and server can live
findings.fact: consensus depends on network and storage (not on chain_sync); chain_sync depends on consensus, network, storage, executor. DagConsensus holds only `p2p_tx: Option<Sender<String>>` as an outbound handle and has no reference to its own Arc<RwLock<_>>; the RwLock is created and owned in main.rs.
findings.evidence: consensus/consensus/Cargo.toml:7-8 `storage = { path = "../../common/storage" } network = { path = "../../common/network" }`; sync/Cargo.toml:9-14 `storage = ... network = ... blockchain = ... consensus = { path = "../consensus/consensus" } crypto = ... executor = ...`; consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:78 `pub p2p_tx: Option<tokio::sync::mpsc::Sender<String>>, // Added P2P Libp2p Channel`; core/node/src/main.rs:602-611 `let consensus = Arc::new(RwLock::new(DagConsensus::new(node_id.clone(), Arc::clone(&peers), ..., p2p_tx_clone, signing_key.to_bytes(),)));`
findings.implication_for_design: Serving belongs in chain_sync (it already owns storage + peers and serves SYNC_REQ) or a sibling module; the client-side fetcher must be spawned from main.rs because it needs Arc<RwLock<DagConsensus>> to inject results. Consensus→fetcher signalling needs a NEW channel field beside p2p_tx (constructor at dag.rs:107-116 and struct init at 438-465), carrying `(missing_hash, citing_author)` tuples; the fetcher then uses network::secure_connect directly (consensus already links network).

findings.topic: Peer liveness maintenance that a fetcher can rely on
findings.fact: A 15 s maintenance loop re-handshakes bootnodes and every saved `peer:` row (pruning Docker-bridge IPs), populating `peers` and `peer_ip`; periodic block sync runs every 3 s and calls reload_chain_tip after progress.
findings.evidence: core/node/src/main.rs:826-828 `println!("🛡️ P2P Maintenance Service started (Auto-Reconnect every 15s)"); loop { tokio::time::sleep(tokio::time::Duration::from_secs(15)).await;` :861-871 `let saved_peers = storage_clone_reconnect.scan_peers(); for (peer_id, peer_port) in saved_peers { ... let ip = storage_clone_reconnect.get_peer_ip(&peer_id).unwrap_or_else(|| "127.0.0.1".to_string());` :1016-1031 `let sync_interval_ms = ... .unwrap_or(3_000); ... loop { tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(sync_interval_ms)).await; ... let synced_height = chain_sync_periodic.sync_from_peers().await;`
findings.implication_for_design: The fetcher should be its own periodic/triggered task in the same style (spawned in main.rs, checks the shutdown flag), iterating `peers` with `get_peer_ip` exactly as sync_from_peers does. Cadence should be faster than the 3 s consensus tick is not required — a hole blocks only commits, not vertex creation — but retries must be spaced so that repeated VERTEX_REQ to the same peer stays far under the 100 msg/s per-connection cutoff (one new connection per request already resets that window).

findings.topic: Reference design: Narwhal synchronizer (pull-by-digest)
findings.fact: Narwhal specifies that a primary which receives a header/certificate referencing parents (or batches) it does not hold does not discard it; it asks the sender for the missing items by digest and only processes the header once its full causal history is available. Vertices/batches are content-addressed, so any holder can serve them and the response is self-validating.
findings.evidence: Danezis, Kokoris-Kogias, Sonnino, Spiegelman — 'Narwhal and Tusk: A DAG-based Mempool and Efficient BFT Consensus', EuroSys 2022, arXiv:2105.11827, §4 (Narwhal core design; header validation requires availability of parents, missing data is synchronized from the referencing peer by digest).
findings.implication_for_design: AINCORE's `Vertex.hash` and `vertex:{hash}` storage give the same content-addressing; the missing piece is exactly the by-digest pull. The Narwhal rule 'ask the sender of the referencing header' maps onto AINCORE as: ask `citing_vertex.author` first (it must hold the parent to have cited it honestly), then other validators; a validator that cites a parent it cannot serve on request is the behavioural signature of case (1).

findings.topic: Complete wiring list for VERTEX_REQ/VERTEX_RESP
findings.fact: Every place a new request/response pair must touch, derived from the read paths above.
findings.evidence: (W1) new message structs — model on sync/src/lib.rs:8-27 SyncRequest/SyncResponse; (W2) server arm — core/node/src/main.rs:788-798 add `msg.starts_with("VERTEX_REQ:")` → new `ChainSync::handle_vertex_request` reading `vertex:{hash}` (storage put site dag.rs:1177), reply written by common/network/src/lib.rs:375-377; (W3) client fetcher task — spawned in core/node/src/main.rs beside the periodic sync (1022-1042), pattern from sync/src/lib.rs:652-712 / da/src/lib.rs:728-757, injects via `node_consensus.write().handle_message("DAG_VERTEX:…")` (main.rs:722-723 style); (W4) trigger — consensus/consensus/src/ordering.rs:697-702 walk_history must return the missing hash; ordering.rs:581-586 and 730-737 propagate; dag.rs:1290-1293 forwards to a new consensus→fetcher channel declared beside dag.rs:78 and threaded through dag.rs:107-116/438-465; (W5) boot hole scan — after dag.rs:385-389 (or first try_commit); (W6) size/rate bounds — reply ≤ 1 MiB (network:239 inbound cap; client read cap network:655 10 MiB), server-side hash-count cap mirroring sync:1216, batch many hashes per frame to respect network:207-233; (W7) per-hash `unknown`/`below_horizon` signal mirroring sync:20-26 and prune condition dag.rs:1806-1809; (W8) gossip prefix lists main.rs:715-719 and 763-767 only if unsolicited VERTEX_RESP pushes are ever allowed (recommend not).
findings.implication_for_design: No storage schema change, no gossip change, no libp2p change is required for a TCP-only pull. The changes concentrate in ordering.rs (surface the hash), dag.rs (channel + trigger), chain_sync (serve), and main.rs (spawn fetcher, dispatch arm).

open_questions: Should VERTEX_REQ serving read only `vertex:{hash}` from storage (lock-free, disk ⊇ memory) or also consult the in-memory `dag` under consensus.read()? The std RwLock is held across block execution (dag.rs:1273-1855), so a storage-only server is strongly preferable; confirm there is no case where a vertex is in `dag` but its put failed (dag.rs:1179 logs and continues).

Which peers does the fetcher ask, and in what order? Candidates: (1) the author of the vertex that cited the missing hash (Narwhal rule), (2) validators in `peers` with a persisted `peer_ip` (sync:626-632 skip rule), (3) all. Inbound-only/NAT validators have no `peer_ip` and cannot be asked directly — is that acceptable, or does a validator need a reachable TCP endpoint as a protocol requirement?

How is 'unobtainable' decided for case (1)? The fetcher can report 'asked K distinct validators holding ≥2/3 stake, all returned unknown, over R retries'; the design still needs a deterministic rule (identical on every node) for what to do with the citing vertex afterwards, or the halt persists. This is outside Track B but the RESP format must carry per-hash `unknown` to make it decidable.

Should walk_history return ALL missing hashes in one pass (bounded by MAX_PARENTS=256 per vertex, dag.rs:37) or just the first? Returning all lets one VERTEX_REQ batch cover the whole hole set but changes a hot path under the consensus lock.

What is the response size policy when a single vertex is near MAX_VERTEX_BYTES (768 KiB)? A batch reply must be trimmed to 1 MiB (or the client's 10 MiB read cap) and the remainder re-requested; confirm the client-side cap the design targets.

Does the fetcher need a boot-time hole scan, or is the commit-path trigger sufficient (first try_commit after boot re-derives the missing hash)? The commit-path trigger only fires for validators (observers return before ordering, dag.rs:1248-1258) — do observers need to fill holes at all, given they follow via adopt_synced_anchor?

Is adding a libp2p request-response behaviour (stable validator→PeerId mapping required; keypair is regenerated per boot, p2p.rs:64) in scope for a later phase, or is direct TCP the permanent transport for pulls?
